18:59 Local Time, 14:59 GMT, 20:29 IST: An exceptional bowling performance from Afghanistan. Yes, it's a used pitch and not the easiest surface to bat on, but this certainly wasn't a 169-all-out wicket. The pacers, Fazalhaq and Omarzai, set the tone by picking up three wickets in the powerplay. Taylor fell soon after, leaving Zimbabwe reeling at 55/4, before Raza and Burl joined forces to steady the innings. The pair rotated the strike well and picked up the odd boundary, but the introduction of Nabi put the brakes on the scoring and eventually led to Burl's dismissal. That opened the door for Rashid Khan, who ran through the lower order, picking up the next three wickets, including the crucial scalp of Raza, who fought a lone battle with a 68. The last wicket stand did frustrate Afghanistan, adding 32 valuable runs, but Zimbabwe have still finished with a below-par total. Afghanistan will back themselves to chase this down. Back in 30 minutes..

Mohammad Nabi: [On the recipe here to take wickets] Yeah, there is no recipe. I only bowl line and length, and according to condition, what's (the team's) need. That's according to condition, I bowled on the right areas. That's why most dot balls, I try to bowl, and then batsman can react a little bit, give me a chance to get the wickets. [On the pitch conditions] Yeah, it's in afternoon a little bit flat. Soon it's sun down, a little bit the weather, a little bit breeze starts, and also the weather condition a little bit change and (the ball) start turning as well. That's more important to assess the condition. [On Afghanistan's confidence in chasing 170] Yeah, we try our best to chase this target.
Welcome back. Last game Afghanistan took their time to chase down 161 against Bangladesh. Can they do it quicker tonight? They should win this game unless Zimbabwe produce something special.
